public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 42: Maximal Sidon Sets and Disjoint Difference Sets

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/42](https://www.erdosproblems.com/42)

This problem asks whether maximal Sidon sets can coexist with other Sidon sets that have
disjoint difference sets (apart from 0).
-/

@[expose] public section

open Function Set Filter
open scoped Pointwise

namespace Erdos42

/--
**Erdős Problem 42**: Let M ≥ 1 and N be sufficiently large in terms of M. Is it true that for every
maximal Sidon set `A ⊆ {1,…,N}` there is another Sidon set `B ⊆ {1,…,N}` of size M such that
`(A - A) ∩ (B - B) = {0}`?

This was proved for all $M$ by GPT 5.5 Pro (prompted by Sandhu), see discussion thread for more details.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5 11, formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/Shashi456/erdos-formalizations/blob/main/Erdos/P42/CompactCayley/Proof.lean"]
theorem erdos_42 : answer(True) ↔
    ∀ M ≥ 1, ∀ᶠ N in atTop, ∀ (A : Set ℕ) (_ : IsMaximalSidonSetIn A N),
    ∃ᵉ (B : Set ℕ), B ⊆ Set.Icc 1 N ∧ IsSidon B ∧ B.ncard = M ∧
    ((A - A) ∩ (B - B)) = {0} := by
  sorry

/--
A variant asking for explicit bounds on how large N needs to be in terms of M.

This version provides a constructive function f such that for all M ≥ 1 and N ≥ f(M),
every maximal Sidon set A ⊆ {1,…,N} has another Sidon set B ⊆ {1,…,N} of size M with
disjoint difference sets (apart from 0).
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5 11,
  formal_proof using formal_conjectures at "https://github.com/KitaKen1/erdos-42-constructive-variant/blob/1f82c76be43cb56f22e2f7f792e392d5fb3ff78c/lean/Erdos42Constructive.lean"]
theorem erdos_42.variants.constructive : answer(True) ↔
    ∃ (f : ℕ → ℕ), ∀ (M N : ℕ) (_ : 1 ≤ M) (_ : f M ≤ N),
    ∀ (A : Set ℕ) (_ : IsMaximalSidonSetIn A N), ∃ᵉ (B : Set ℕ),
      B ⊆ Set.Icc 1 N ∧ IsSidon B ∧ B.ncard = M ∧
      ((A - A) ∩ (B - B)) = {0} := by
  sorry


/-  ## Related results and examples -/

/--
The set `{1, 2, 4}` is a maximal Sidon set in `{1, ..., 4}`.
-/
@[category textbook, AMS 5 11]
theorem example_maximal_sidon : IsMaximalSidonSetIn {1, 2, 4} 4 := by
  refine ⟨?_, ?_, ?_⟩
  · intro x hx
    simp only [Set.mem_insert_iff, Set.mem_singleton_iff] at hx
    rcases hx with rfl | rfl | rfl <;> simp [Set.mem_Icc]
  · intro i₁ hi₁ j₁ hj₁ i₂ hi₂ j₂ hj₂ hsum
    simp only [Set.mem_insert_iff, Set.mem_singleton_iff] at hi₁ hj₁ hi₂ hj₂
    rcases hi₁ with rfl | rfl | rfl <;>
    rcases hj₁ with rfl | rfl | rfl <;>
    rcases hi₂ with rfl | rfl | rfl <;>
    rcases hj₂ with rfl | rfl | rfl <;>
    simp_all
  · intro x hx hxA
    simp only [Set.mem_Icc] at hx; obtain ⟨hx1, hx2⟩ := hx
    simp only [Set.mem_insert_iff, Set.mem_singleton_iff, not_or] at hxA
    obtain ⟨hne1, hne2, hne4⟩ := hxA
    have hx3 : x = 3 := (by omega); subst hx3
    intro hbad
    have := hbad 1 (by simp) 2 (by simp) 3 (by simp) 2 (by simp) (by norm_num)
    rcases this with ⟨h1, h2⟩ | ⟨h1, h2⟩ <;> omega

/--
The difference set of `{1, 2, 4}` is `{0, 1, 2, 3}`.
-/
@[category textbook, AMS 5 11]
theorem example_difference_set : ({1, 2, 4} : Set ℕ) - {1, 2, 4} = {0, 1, 2, 3} := by
  ext x
  simp only [Set.mem_sub, Set.mem_insert_iff, Set.mem_singleton_iff]
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨a, ha, b, hb, rfl⟩
    rcases ha with rfl | rfl | rfl <;>
    rcases hb with rfl | rfl | rfl <;>
    simp
  · rintro (rfl | rfl | rfl | rfl)
    · exact ⟨1, by decide, 1, by decide, by decide⟩
    · exact ⟨2, by decide, 1, by decide, by decide⟩
    · exact ⟨4, by decide, 2, by decide, by decide⟩
    · exact ⟨4, by decide, 1, by decide, by decide⟩

/--
For any maximal Sidon set, the difference set contains 0.
-/
@[category textbook, AMS 5 11]
theorem maximal_sidon_contains_zero (A : Set ℕ) (N : ℕ) (hN : 1 ≤ N)
    (hA : IsMaximalSidonSetIn A N) : 0 ∈ A - A := by
  obtain ⟨hAsub, hAsidon, hAmax⟩ := hA
  have hne : A.Nonempty
  · by_contra hemp; rw [Set.not_nonempty_iff_eq_empty] at hemp
    exact hAmax (Set.mem_Icc.mpr ⟨le_refl 1, hN⟩)
      (by rw [hemp]; exact id) (by
        rw [hemp, Set.empty_union]
        exact fun _ hi _ hj _ hk _ hl _ => by
          simp only [Set.mem_singleton_iff] at hi hj hk hl
          subst hi
          subst hj
          subst hk
          subst hl
          exact Or.inl ⟨rfl, rfl⟩)
  obtain ⟨a, ha⟩ := hne
  have := Set.sub_mem_sub ha ha
  rwa [Nat.sub_self] at this

end Erdos42

findings.description: The docstring promises “explicit bounds” and says the theorem “provides a constructive function f.” The Lean statement only asserts `∃ f : ℕ → ℕ` satisfying the threshold property. It specifies neither a numerical bound nor any computability requirement; by classical choice it is equivalent to the main theorem's eventual statement. The qualitative mathematics is faithful, but the docstring overstates what this variant formalizes.
findings.source_evidence: The exact linked proof, https://raw.githubusercontent.com/KitaKen1/erdos-42-constructive-variant/1f82c76be43cb56f22e2f7f792e392d5fb3ff78c/lean/Erdos42Constructive.lean, explicitly says: “Classical choice selects one threshold for each M” and “This is an existence proof. It does not compute an explicit numerical bound.” The problem at https://www.erdosproblems.com/42 asks for sufficiently large N in terms of M; its separate quantitative remark is not stated by this declaration.
findings.suggested_fix: Describe this as an equivalent threshold-function formulation of the main theorem, removing the promises of explicit bounds and constructivity. No change to the qualitative theorem is necessary. If an explicit-bound variant is intended instead, state a specified quantitative bound.

reformulations.difference: The file uses sets of natural numbers and truncated natural-number subtraction instead of ordinary integer difference sets. The constructive variant uses the same convention.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: An integer self-difference set is symmetric under negation. Its nonnegative part is exactly the natural-number self-difference set after embedding the original set into ℤ, including at zero and for empty sets. Consequently, the natural-number intersection equals {0} if and only if the integer intersection equals {0}. This exact equivalence for arbitrary A and B was proved as Review42.nat_int_difference_iff in the scratch file.

reformulations.difference: The current source says “every Sidon set,” while Lean quantifies only over inclusion-maximal Sidon subsets of the interval.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Every Sidon subset of a finite interval extends to an inclusion-maximal Sidon subset C. A companion avoiding the nonzero differences of C also avoids those of A ⊆ C. For nonempty A, zero remains in both difference sets, so the required equality is preserved. Conversely, maximal sets are nonempty when N ≥ 1, which holds eventually. The source's mathematical discussion explicitly states the nonempty formulation (post 6069) and the inclusion-maximal extension argument (post 6107); post 2050 calls maximality a without-loss-of-generality restriction. The extension lemma and eventual equivalence were proved in Lean as Review42.sidon_has_maximal_extension and Review42.eventual_maximal_vs_all.

reformulations.difference: Instead of an eventual-in-N statement for each positive M, this declaration existentially quantifies one threshold function f : ℕ → ℕ.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: On ℕ, `∀ᶠ N in atTop, P M N` means that some threshold n₀ works for every N ≥ n₀. Classical choice selects such a threshold for each positive M, with an arbitrary value at M = 0. Conversely, any witnessing function immediately supplies the eventual threshold. Review42.threshold_iff proves this equivalence for arbitrary P. Thus the declaration is a faithful qualitative reformulation, not a stronger quantitative result.

sources_consulted: http://erdosproblems.com/forum/discuss/42 — mathematical discussion, particularly posts 2050, 6069, 6107, and 6112; repository-file discussion was excluded
review.notes: All five declarations were checked. No mathematical misformalization was found. The source records a positive solution for all M, verified in Lean, consistent with both `research solved` tags and both `answer(True)` values. The three auxiliary theorems have only standard axioms, with no sorryAx. Scratch checks compiled successfully in /workspace/review/scratch.lean, including the equivalences, N = 0 and N = 1 cases, a general M = 1 witness, and finite computations through N = 8. Both A and B lie in finite intervals, so ncard's infinite-set default cannot affect the statements. The external proof statements were inspected; the long standalone proof did not replay unchanged because it targets Lean/Mathlib 4.27.0 while this sandbox uses 4.33.1. That API-compatibility limitation is not evidence of a stale or incorrect proof-status record.
